one_liner: Rust/Python (PyO3) vision library whose NEON u8 resize and colour kernels beat OpenCV bilinear resize on aarch64 Jetson.
what_it_does: kornia-rs is a Rust computer-vision workspace (kornia-image, kornia-imgproc, kornia-io and others) shipped as crates, a PyO3 wheel (pip install kornia-rs) and C++ bindings. For resampling, kornia_imgproc::resize::resize_fast_u8_aa resizes u8 images with 1, 3 or 4 channels (nearest, bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos3) and takes an antialias flag. The colour module converts f32 RGB to gray, HSV, HLS, XYZ, Lab, Luv, YCbCr, YUV and Bayer formats. From Python, kornia_rs.image.Image.resize(width, height, interpolation="bilinear", antialias=True) and kornia_rs.imgproc.resize(img, (h, w), interpolation) wrap numpy buffers without copying and return numpy arrays. This is a different API, not a drop-in for cv2.resize or cv2.cvtColor.
how_it_is_fast: A dispatch cascade sends special cases to dedicated kernels. An exact 2x bilinear downscale becomes a 2x2 box average (NEON vpaddlq_u8 plus vrshrn), and an exact 2x upscale uses fixed {0.25, 0.75} weights computed with vrhaddq_u8 pairs. General bilinear precomputes Q14 tap LUTs per column and spreads 16-row chunks across rayon threads; the per-row loop itself is scalar. Bicubic and Lanczos3 follow the Pillow-style separable two-pass Q14 convolution: an i16 intermediate, u16 column LUTs, a 4-row NEON horizontal kernel that shares coefficient loads, and an L2-aware strip-fused H-then-V plan. antialias=False fixes the taps at 4 or 6 instead of widening them with the scale. The f32 colour kernels deinterleave with vld3q, apply the 3x3 matrix in registers, and use a degree-4 log2 / degree-3 exp2 pow and a one-iteration Halley cbrt (about 4e-4 and 2.3e-5 relative error).
when_to_use: Python or Rust pipelines on aarch64 edge boards (Jetson Orin, Raspberry Pi 5, Apple silicon) that call cv2.resize INTER_LINEAR on u8 RGB frames. The Orin page shows 1.55-1.97x at 1080p to 540p and 3.09x at 640 to 320, plus 5.52x on an exact 2x upscale, where the output is slightly biased (see gotchas).
Model-input preprocessing: resize_normalize_to_tensor fuses resize, /255, mean/std and HWC-to-CHW into one pass to f32, replacing a cv2-plus-numpy chain; a CUDA Preprocessor does the same on device.

Replacing Pillow LANCZOS or BICUBIC with the same antialiased semantics on ARM, where Pillow-SIMD has no NEON path: kornia's antialiased Lanczos is 3.1-5.3x faster than Pillow 12.2.0 on the Orin (derived from page data).
RGB to Lab in f32 where colour-grade precision is enough: 1.35-1.55x faster than cv2.cvtColor, and closer to true Lab than OpenCV's LUT-interpolated f32 path, according to the page.
Free-threaded CPython (3.13t/3.14t) or GIL-free Rust services that want thread-safe image ops with numpy and DLPack zero-copy.
when_not_to_use: Antialiased (default) bicubic or Lanczos downscaling as a cv2 replacement: it is slower than OpenCV on the page's own matrix, Lanczos at 0.64-0.87x and bicubic AA at 0.55-0.85x. Its antialias=False Lanczos is 3-lobe (6 taps) against OpenCV's 8-tap INTER_LANCZOS4, so even those wins do less work.

x86-64: there are no published x86 numbers. The general bilinear row kernel is scalar on every architecture, the exact-2x downscale and upscale row kernels are scalar off aarch64, and the CIE colour kernels fall back to scalar under AVX2. Issue #667 (January 2026, open, hardware unstated, predates the April-June 2026 tuning) reported bilinear resize 1.7-4.9x slower than OpenCV.

Pipelines that need byte-for-byte OpenCV output: bicubic uses a = -0.5 (Pillow) while OpenCV INTER_CUBIC uses A = -0.75, Lanczos has 3 lobes against OpenCV's 4, Lab and Luv differ by up to 0.67, and the exact-2x upscale is biased.
Non-u8 resizing (f32/u16 fast resize is the open issue #862), and HSV, HLS, Luv or YCbCr conversions, where kornia is at parity or slower than cv2 (0.61-1.08x across the page's two colour tables).

Codec speed claims from the same bake-off: JPEG is a tie (libjpeg-turbo on all sides). In the 23x WebP row, cv2.imencode('.webp') with no parameters actually runs lossless libwebp (OpenCV grfmt_webp.cpp falls back to lossless when no quality is given), which contradicts the page's 'lossy' note; PIL's is lossy. File sizes are not reported, and PNG level 1 is set against PIL's default level.

integration.form: crate (kornia or kornia-imgproc), plus a PyO3 wheel (kornia-rs on PyPI) and C++ bindings (kornia-cpp)
integration.dependencies: kornia-imgproc: rayon, wide, num-traits, thiserror, kornia-image/-tensor/-algebra; optional cudarc and half (cuda feature). Python wheel: numpy; turbojpeg (needs nasm to build) on by default in kornia-py
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (workspace rust-version); Python 3.8-3.14 including free-threaded builds; maturin >= 1.9 to build the wheel
integration.platforms: aarch64 NEON first (Linux incl. Jetson, macOS, Windows arm64); x86-64 with AVX2 for some resize kernels (blend, separable H/V passes) chosen at run time, scalar elsewhere; wheels for manylinux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, win_amd64/arm64; optional CUDA path loaded lazily
integration.thread_safety: The README says it is thread-safe, including under free-threaded Python. Each call runs internally across the global rayon pool, so concurrent callers share those threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it accepts numpy u8 arrays and returns numpy, but the API, argument order (imgproc.resize takes (h, w), cv2 takes (w, h)), defaults (antialias=True) and kernels differ from cv2.resize and Pillow

gotchas: The exact-2x bilinear upscale fast path (the 5.52x row) computes 0.75a+0.25b as rhadd(a, rhadd(a, b)) in both passes and requantizes to u8 between them. The code comment says this equals round(0.75a+0.25b), but double rounding always rounds up: a pure-Python replay of the scalar reference on random u8 input gave a +0.74 LSB mean bias against float64 bilinear, with 71% of pixels 1 LSB above the correctly rounded value (max 1 LSB). The unit test checks only the four corner pixels, and bench_resize_vs_libs.py has no 2x-upscale case, so a 1920x1080 to 3840x2160 resize comes out slightly brighter than a 3838-wide one, which takes the general Q14 path.

Image.resize on 1- or 4-channel images silently ignores the interpolation argument and runs a floor-convention nearest-neighbour resize. Only 3-channel input reaches the bilinear, bicubic and Lanczos kernels.

Image.resize defaults to interpolation="bilinear", antialias=True. The page's '1080p->720p (Lanczos)' bake-off row actually ran this bilinear default against cv2 INTER_LANCZOS4 and PIL LANCZOS, so it says nothing about Lanczos speed.

The rust doc of xyz_from_rgb says it gamma-decodes, but the kernel is matrix-only (to match cv2 COLOR_RGB2XYZ), so it is not colorimetric sRGB-to-XYZ; use linear_rgb_from_rgb first if you need that. The bicubic/Lanczos column LUT is u16, guarded only by a debug_assert, so release builds would silently wrap source columns for images wider than 65,535 px.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick kornia-rs on aarch64 (Python or Rust) when you want numpy-in, numpy-out, multi-threaded bilinear resize and colour conversion that beats cv2 there, with optional CUDA dispatch. Pick fast_image_resize for antialiased convolution resizing in Rust on x86-64 AVX2 (single-thread, beats libvips), Pillow-SIMD for antialiased resizing in Python on x86, and OpenCV itself for bicubic/Lanczos downscales or byte-exact cv2 output.
verified_claims_summary: These are first-party numbers from kornia-py/benchmarks.md on a Jetson Orin (Cortex-A78AE, 6 cores, Rust 1.93.0 at opt-level=2, OpenCV 4.13.0 at default threads, Pillow 12.2.0), best-of-N minimum on random 1080p RGB u8, run at commit 07e52d7, which is not on GitHub. The like-for-like bilinear comparison against cv2 INTER_LINEAR shows 1.55-1.97x at 1080p to 540p, 1.33x (derived from page data) to 2.84x at 1080p to 224x224, 3.09x to 4.1x (derived from page data) at 640 to 320, and 5.52x on the exact-2x upscale. Each range spans the matrix's aa=True and aa=False columns, which run identical code because antialias does not affect bilinear, so the spread is run-to-run noise. The 2x-upscale output carries a +0.74 LSB rounding bias that the page does not disclose.
status_note: Actively developed: 1,001 commits, v0.2.0 released 2026-09-26, last commit 2026-09-27, 720 stars, kornia-imgproc at about 47.6k crates.io downloads. Apache-2.0 and usable as a crate or a wheel, but the speed work targets aarch64 first.
